newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says race stand correct - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says race stand correct - spokesman.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard stood by his response to the current racism debate, a Liberal-National spokesman said on Tuesday.

"He said that he believed that the approach he had taken over this matter was one which was correct and he wasn't proposing to change that approach," the spokesman told reporters. "I should say that there was widespread support by way of affirmation in the party room to that."
Howard also denied that an outbreak of racism was engulfing Australia, saying the community was hearing only a few voices.
"He also referred to some attempts to try and paint the coalition as being soft in relation to these issues," he said.
"He said we will continue to choose the forum in which we make remarks and we will be making them positively."
Howard said Australia did need to have a debate about immigration levels but the policy would remain non-discriminatory.
Australian opposition leader Kim Beazley called Tuesday for the government to counteract the bad publicity it was getting in Asia over the racism debate.

Australia became embroiled in a heated debate over immigration and race last month after Independent politician Pauline Hanson said the country was being swamped by Asians and called for an end to immigration.
Howard has been criticised for not taking a more definite stand on the issue.
